subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` make only the isolated sandbox-owned `/workspace` writable, and which Docker, local bridge, remote bridge, tool-exposure, docs, and test surfaces must change together?
rationale: The source fix shape is clear, but the change modifies a security-owned sandbox write boundary and overlaps adjacent custom-bind policy work, so automation should not choose the permanent contract by itself.

options.title: Approve Isolated Writable None
options.body: Implement writable `none` only for the sandbox-owned workspace while preserving real workspace isolation, read-only skill overlays, and bridge path guards.

options.title: Keep None Fully Read-Only
options.body: Document `none` as no writable workspace and resolve the user-facing failure by hiding or explaining write-capable tools instead.

options.title: Defer To Broader Bind Policy
options.body: Pause this bug until maintainers decide the related writable custom-bind model, accepting that existing `none` sandbox writes remain broken meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Approve Isolated Writable None
recommendation.body: Implement writable `none` only for the sandbox-owned workspace while preserving real workspace isolation, read-only skill overlays, and bridge path guards.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the behavior now under debate and posted the latest related maintainer decision keeping this issue as canonical.
